extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — grant applicants, administrators, and investigators
extracted.subtask_description: A news index summarizing recent NIH extramural policy, process, and resource updates for investigators and grant applicants. It alerts readers to new formats, initiatives, review-process changes, and informational resources relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate models for research (including New Approach Methodologies)
rubrics_metrics.description: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose models (including NAMs) based on scientific appropriateness and fit to the research question; NIH encourages human-relevant and translational approaches but emphasizes selecting the best model for the question rather than adopting methods solely because they are new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applicable submissions, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified in that format; the announcement signals an expectation to follow the new template for pilot-plan submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility across NIH research
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees should incorporate considerations of replication and reproducibility in study design, methods, and planning where appropriate; expect NIH initiatives and highlighted topics to prioritize and potentially influence review and funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that some applications deemed competitive may not be discussed in study section under modified review processes; this designation reflects triage thresholds and procedural changes (e.g., emergency modifications) and affects how applicants interpret scores and possible next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 Collaborative International Research Project application format and post-review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PF5 submissions, follow the specific application format and be prepared for administrative actions after review (such as splitting into linked awards prior to JIT); use NIH overview resources to learn required features and format details.
